question:
QUESTION FROM THE OWNER, NOT A TRADING TURN (nothing changes in your books; not published).

The site's Scoreboard (in the header on every page) ranks the best results across all three AIs and all races: up to 12 lines (the ten races plus the two All in side races), best first.

The owner proposes: on Home, keep the Scoreboard exactly as it is (all races). But when a visitor leaves Home and opens a specific section (for example the Sports tab, or Crypto, or All in), the Scoreboard switches to show only that section: the three AIs ranked in that one race (e.g. a "Sports scoreboard" with 1st, 2nd, 3rd), so the header always matches the page being viewed. Going back to Home shows the full Scoreboard again.

Is this a good idea? Majority wins.

Reply in this exact shape, short:
VOTE: YES or NO - one sentence why
NOTE: one thing to get right if it is built (optional, one sentence)

chatgpt.answer:
VOTE: YES - It makes the header more relevant to the page while Home still preserves the full overall ranking.
NOTE: Clearly label the scope so visitors don’t confuse section rankings with the overall Scoreboard.

gemini.answer:
VOTE: YES - Showing section-specific rankings reduces header clutter and provides immediately relevant context for the page the user is actually viewing.
NOTE: Ensure the scoreboard title dynamically updates (e.g., "Sports Scoreboard") so visitors clearly understand they are looking at filtered results rather than the global rankings.
